## Coagulation of cloud into precipitation (`type: coagulation`) {#sec-ch06-coagulation}

### Summary

Coagulation converts one condensed species into another, typically cloud into precipitation (autoconversion). It
uses the Arrhenius rate form of @sec-ch06-arrhenius, including its bands and its pressure switch, but every species
it names is registered as a cloud species rather than a vapor.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** First-order conversion $r = k\, c_{\mathrm{cloud}}$ with $k$ from @eq-ch06-arrhenius-rate.

**Data.** As @sec-ch06-arrhenius; reactants and products are condensed species.

**Placement.** Second evaluator of `Kinetics.forward`.

**Activation.** `type: coagulation`; the keys of `type: arrhenius`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Conserves moles of condensate for one-to-one reactions.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

The options class derives from the Arrhenius options and changes only the reaction type it reads.

### Derivation

The rate is @eq-ch06-mass-action-rate with $k_j$ from @eq-ch06-arrhenius-rate; for $\mathrm{A(s)} \to
\mathrm{A(s,p)}$ it is $r = k\, c_{\mathrm{A(s)}}$. A closed box at fixed $p$ then has
$x_c(t) = x_{c0}\, e^{-k t}$, the closed form the test integrates against. No other derivation is needed.

### Numerical method

`reset` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}}) registers the coagulation options with the
Arrhenius evaluator; nothing else differs from @sec-ch06-arrhenius.

The figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Limits

No test of a coagulation reaction with more than one reactant. Not measured.
